question: How does one network learn both a conditional and an unconditional noise predictor in classifier-free guidance?
options: The label is replaced by a null token for a random fraction of training examples
A classifier is trained on noisy images
The unconditional model is computed by averaging over all labels at sampling time
explanation: Label dropout (20% here) teaches the same weights eps(x_t, t, null).

question: In image generation tools, what does raising the guidance scale usually do?
options: Makes images follow the prompt more strongly, at the cost of variety
explanation: It sharpens the distribution toward the condition.

question: Which guidance scale reproduces the true conditional distribution p(x | y)?
explanation: At s = 1 the guided eps is eps_c; the script shows the best fidelity (sliced W 0.038) and 95% class adherence, like real data.

question: What does eps_c - eps_u correspond to?
options: A scaled gradient of log p(y | x), an implicit classifier
explanation: By Bayes, grad log p(x | y) - grad log p(x) = grad log p(y | x).

question: At scale 8 every sample is classified as class 0, yet the sliced W to real class 0 is the worst. Why?
options: Samples crowd into the most certain part of the class, losing diversity and no longer matching the real conditional distribution
explanation: Guidance samples from roughly p(x) p(y | x)^s, a narrower distribution than p(x | y).

question: Why do implementations stack conditional and unconditional inputs into one batch?
options: It changes the result in a useful way
It is required by the math
It computes the same two predictions in one forward pass, which is faster on parallel hardware
It removes the need for the null token
explanation: The script shows a max difference of exactly 0 between the two ways.
